data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's primary claim states resumption is safe iff (1) the last event is complete, (2) the causal fingerprint matches, and (3) no intermediate event declares logical incompleteness (e.g., a 'begin' without a matching 'commit'). If token-budget exhaustion interrupts mid-event, a 'begin' without a 'commit' is permanently written into the append-only log. Because the log is append-only, this intermediate event cannot be removed or rewritten; thus condition (3) is permanently violated. The target's primary 'iff' criterion therefore makes resumption permanently impossible after any mid-event interruption, failing to identify when resumption may safely occur. While its auxiliary counterconditions mention 'explicit resume markers' as a special case satisfying criterion 3, this is not integrated into the main adjudication criteria, leaving the core conjunction overly restrictive and incapable of adjudicating safe append-only recovery via abort markers.
